_datum: Origin = the back corner of the MAIN table top on the side AWAY FROM THE RETURN. +x runs along the main table TOWARD the return, +y runs out from the back wall toward where you stand, +z is up off the table top (below the bench is -z). Everything on the bench is positive in all three.
_handedness: The return is a LEFT-HAND return: standing at the main table facing the back wall, it is on your left. Facing -y with +z up gives right = -x, so your left is +x - which is why the return sits at HIGH x and the origin corner is the one on your RIGHT. This was modelled mirrored on 2026-07-26 and only the 3D render caught it; the ASCII plan hid it completely.
_measured: 2026-07-26, Kyle: main run, return, 3/4 in ply top. Unmeasured values are null ON PURPOSE - the twin models only what is measured and reports the rest as absent, because a guessed obstacle is worse than a missing one (the gate would report CLEAR against a fiction).

surfaces.name: main
surfaces.notes: the long run across the back

surfaces.name: return
surfaces.notes: LEFT-hand return (high x), forward of the main run. Kyle CORRECTED 2026-07-26: from the back wall it runs 27.5 (main table depth) + 34 = 61.5 to a seam, then 72 more to the end. Total depth from the back edge is 133.5, so this surface spans y 27.5..133.5 = 106 deep. The earlier 76 was wrong.

features.name: return_seam
features.notes: Where the return's two tops meet, 61.5 from the back wall (27.5 + 34). A 2x4 LEG lands here - it is below the table top (-z) so it cannot be reached by the arm, but it is recorded now so it is not forgotten. Details pending from Kyle.

_walls_note: height is USABLE HEIGHT ABOVE THE TABLE TOP, not floor to ceiling - the arm can only ever reach what is above the surface it is bolted to. yaw_deg is the direction the wall RUNS: 0 = along +x, 90 = along +y. outward is the direction the wall MATERIAL sits from its face. ROUGHED IN 2026-07-26 at Kyle's direction, pending real measurement: both heights are 'about 3 usable feet' and the corner gap is a placeholder.

walls.name: back
walls.notes: Runs along the back edge of the main table, stopping 8.25 short of the side wall (82 - 8.25 = 73.75) to leave the corner gap. Height still ROUGH at 'about 3 usable feet'.

walls.name: side
walls.notes: Runs the full length of the return, end to end, on the LEFT as you face the back wall (high x in datum coords). Length follows the corrected return: 133.5 from the back wall. Height still ROUGH.

corner_gap._comment: Gap in the corner between the back wall and the side wall. Kyle measured it 2026-07-26 at 8.25, replacing the 6 placeholder. Modelled as the back wall stopping 8.25 short of the side wall, so the gap spans x 73.75..82.

arm._comment: Where the arm's base centre sits on the table, in datum coords, and which way it faces. yaw_deg is the direction the arm points with m1 at 0 deg: 0 = toward the front of the desk (+y), positive counter-clockwise viewed from above (so +90 points along -x). SAFETY-CRITICAL: switching the twin from its infinite ground plane to the real finite tabletop makes the gate LESS conservative - it will believe there is air past the table edge. A wrong arm position therefore means the gate can call CLEAR over real tabletop. Until x/y/yaw_deg are measured the twin keeps the infinite plane.
